trading_tips: Risk only 1 to 2 percent of your capital on any single trade. Size positions so that a stopped-out trade is a minor cost, not a portfolio event.
Always place a stop-loss when you enter a trade, and honour it. Deciding the exit after the loss starts is how small losses become large ones.

Treat F&O with extra caution after the Budget 2026 STT hike: from 1 April 2026, STT is 0.05% on futures (up from 0.02%), 0.15% on options premium (up from 0.10%), and 0.15% on exercised options (up from 0.125%). Higher costs punish frequent trading, and SEBI data shows most retail F&O traders lose money.
Never trade on tips from WhatsApp, Telegram or finfluencers. Verify every idea against company filings and exchange disclosures, and consult a SEBI-registered investment adviser.

Penny stocks under Rs 100 carry manipulation and liquidity risk. Check daily volumes before buying, keep total penny exposure to 10 to 15 percent of the portfolio, and exit slowly because your own sell orders move the price.
Separate investing from trading: use SIPs in diversified funds for long-term goals, keep a 6-month emergency fund untouched, and never fund trading with borrowed money.
Track the macro dashboard weekly: FII/DII flows, Brent crude, USD/INR, India VIX and RBI policy signals move Indian markets more than headlines do.
